thesis: City of Brass made every color available from one land and asked players to price perfect mana in points of life, a bargain that enabled strategies conventional mana bases could not support.

competitiveTimeline.significance: The land appears across early multicolor control, combo, Five-Color, Dredge, and tournament mana bases that valued access over comfort, making it one of Magic’s foundational fixing designs.

playbook.role: Use City when color access is worth more than incremental life, and sequence other lands first when they can cast the same spell without damage. In combo turns, count every activation before committing to a line.

counterplay.directAnswers: Pressure life totals so each activation matters, use effects that force repeated tapping, and exploit the fact that City cannot provide painless mana in a race. Mana denial is strongest when the deck has few alternative colored sources.
